paper.title: Thompson Sampling for Learning in Zero-Sum Games

settings.name_in_paper: Centralized self-play in unknown two-player zero-sum matrix game with Gaussian bandit feedback (unique NE)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learning in games with an equilibrium (Nash duality gap) objective.
unmapped: arms are entries of an m x n payoff matrix; learner picks mixed strategies (x_t, y_t) for both players and observes noisy payoff of sampled pair (I_t,J_t)
performance measured by cumulative duality gap sum_t Gap(x_t,y_t)
payoff matrix assumed to have a unique Nash equilibrium
settings.definition_quote: At each round t=1,...,T, the learner chooses both x_t and y_t ... observes the selected action pair (I_t,J_t) and receives only its noisy payoff Y_t=A^*_{I_tJ_t}+xi_t, xi_t ~ N(0,sigma^2), where the noise variance sigma^2>0 is known. ... R_T(A) := sum_t Gap_A(x_t,y_t).

settings.name_in_paper: Zero-sum matrix game with Gaussian bandit feedback (lower bound)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learning in games with an equilibrium (Nash duality gap) objective.
unmapped: arms are entries of a payoff matrix; learner controls both players' mixed strategies
performance measured by cumulative duality gap
settings.definition_quote: Consider any possibly randomized, nonanticipating policy pi for the learning protocol in Section 3. The policy may depend on (m,R,sigma,T) but not on the unknown payoff matrix.

symbols.C_mix: instance constant depending on (A*,sigma,m,n), O(d sqrt(log(ed))), zero for pure NE
symbols.C_out: instance constant, O(d(m+n-2d)(1+log(mn))^3), zero for fully mixed NE

conditions: A* has a unique Nash equilibrium

source.label: thm:unique-rate
source.quote: Suppose that $m,n\ge2$, $T>mn$, and $A^\star$ has a unique Nash equilibrium. Then, there exist finite nonnegative constants $C_{\rm mix},C_{\rm out},C_0$, depending only on $(A^\star,\sigma,m,n)$, such that Nash-TS satisfies $\E[\mathcal R_T]\le C_{\rm mix}\sqrt T+C_{\rm out}\log(eT)+C_0$. Moreover, $C_{\rm mix}=0$ when the unique equilibrium is pure, and $C_{\rm out}=0$ when it is fully mixed.

results.notes: Quantity is expected cumulative duality gap. Requires solving a Nash equilibrium (LP) each round.

conditions: A* has a unique pure Nash equilibrium

source.label: thm:unique-rate
source.quote: Moreover, $C_{\rm mix}=0$ when the unique equilibrium is pure, and $C_{\rm out}=0$ when it is fully mixed.

symbols.Lambda_core: expected first-order duality gap of the Gaussian core perturbation W^core with variances 2 sigma^2/(x_i* y_j*); zero iff NE pure

conditions: A* has a unique Nash equilibrium

source.label: thm:exact-core-asymptotics
source.quote: Suppose that $m,n\ge2$ and $A^\star$ has a unique Nash equilibrium. Then, Nash-TS satisfies $\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\E[\mathcal R_T]}{\sqrt T}=2\Lambda_{\rm core}$. Moreover, $\Lambda_{\rm core}=0$ when the unique Nash equilibrium is pure, whereas $\Lambda_{\rm core}>0$ otherwise.

results.notes: Exact limit; recorded also as matching lower (liminf) result r4.

symbols.Lambda_core: core asymptotic constant, >0 iff NE not pure

conditions: A* has a unique Nash equilibrium

source.label: thm:exact-core-asymptotics
source.quote: Then, Nash-TS satisfies $\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\E[\mathcal R_T]}{\sqrt T}=2\Lambda_{\rm core}$.

results.notes: Algorithm-specific lower bound for Nash-TS (Theta(sqrt T) for non-pure NE).

conditions: unique Nash equilibrium, not pure, uniform on its supports (x_i*=y_j*=1/d)

source.label: cor:core-coefficient-bound
source.quote: Moreover, if the equilibrium is uniform on its supports, so that $x_i^\star=y_j^\star=1/d$ ... $\frac{3\sqrt2}{8}\sigma\sqrt{d\log d}\le\Lambda_{\rm core}\le4\sigma\sqrt{d\log d}$.

results.notes: Combined with Theorem 5.2 (limit = 2 Lambda_core). Corollary also gives general bound Lambda_core <= 2 sigma sqrt(log d)[(min y*)^{-1/2}+(min x*)^{-1/2}] and lower bound (3 sqrt2/8) sigma sqrt(d log d) in the uniform case.

conditions: hard instance in [-R,R]^{m x m} has a unique fully mixed Nash equilibrium

source.label: thm:unique-minimax-lower
source.quote: For every policy $\pi$ described above and every $T\ge1$, there exists a matrix $A_{\pi,T}\in[-R,R]^{m\times m}$ with a unique fully mixed Nash equilibrium such that $\E_{A_{\pi,T}}^\pi[\mathcal R_T(A_{\pi,T})]\ge\frac1{8192}\min\left\{\frac{RT}{m},\sigma\sqrt{mT\log m}\right\}.$

results.notes: Minimax lower bound on expected cumulative duality gap.

conditions: separable game A*_ij = u_i + v_j with u_1>u_i (i>1), v_1<v_j (j>1): unique pure NE (e_1,e_1)
policy uniformly efficient (o(T^alpha) for all alpha>0) on A* and on separable alternatives

source.label: thm:pure-separable-lower
source.quote: Every policy $\pi$ described above satisfies $\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\E_{A^\star}^\pi[\mathcal R_T(A^\star)]}{\log T}\ge2\sigma^2\left(\sum_{i=2}^m\frac1{u_1-u_i}+\sum_{j=2}^n\frac1{v_j-v_1}\right).

results.notes: Change-of-measure (Lai-Robbins style) lower bound; m,n here are the paper's numbers of row/column actions.
